title: A liquid metal dynamic wetting strategy for spatiotemporal monitoring of hand movements
core_idea: Introduce a flexible, wearable inertial-skeletal tracking (fwist) approach that embeds miniature PDMS microchannels filled with liquid metal. Changes in tilt and angular motion drive migration of the gas–liquid interface and wetting dynamics (influenced by an oxide layer and microstructured channel walls), producing measurable resistance changes. By mounting compact fwist units on bone locations rather than joints, the system transduces palm pitch/roll and phalange bending into electrical signals to enable spatiotemporal reconstruction of hand movements while avoiding visual occlusion and electromagnetic-interference limitations of existing methods.
tldr: A wearable hand-tracking system that uses liquid-metal dynamic wetting inside microchannels on bone-mounted PDMS units to convert tilt and finger bending into electrical signals for robust spatiotemporal monitoring of hand motion.
